By when do you think all the long term debt will be completely paid off by the company by when, when will be the company be free from long term debt because we see total long term debt at 3000 odd crore in the balance sheet.
Growth & demand: This is something that you need 24 hours a day and power demand you can see is only going up and up which was obviously there, but what has happened was that in the rush of private players coming into power sector there was a bit of excess capacity which has all been absorbed right now.
So on a broad basis, we know that this is because of power demand.
So, you can imagine and that was basically because the country was remotely lockdown at that time and power demand went to all-time low.
Margins & costs: So our EBITDA if you see has been stable around +1000 crores since 2015 till 2023 to 2024 now.
It has been +1000 crore EBITDA plant, what was required to be done was only correcting the debt site, which was done in 2020.
So, that would be in the range of we can work out the exact numbers but around 500 crores our cost is about 16% So, you can work out the math there.
Capex & expansion: The remaining three units were commissioned in 2015, March 2015, the entire plant was commissioned these are BHEL units 270x5.
On the operation side, the plant has been a very well performing plant from 2000 ever since it was commissioned in 2015.

Balance sheet & cash: And after that, Jan 2020 debt side was, debt stack was restructured and since then, plant has been a great performing plant.
And in future also that money will surely come and for us that number is north of almost +2500 crore, so that money will also come so that will only add to the cash flows.

See all of Sinnar debt has gone with Sinnar company so that is the bottom line, whatever debt was there on Sinnar and you know that it was 1350 megawatt plant which is similar in size to Amravati, so the principle debt was there, that was about Rs.7000 crores, which was accumulated interest, et cetera, et cetera.

The Amravati Plant achieved a PLF of 82.10% and a Plant Availability Factor of 87.88% for the year, keeping capacity charge recovery on track despite some planned and unplanned outages during the year.

The Amravati Plant maintained an annual Plant Availability Factor of 87.88% and a Plant Load Factor of 82.10% during FY 2025-26, consistent with the provisions of its PPA and enabling the Company to realise 100% of its fixed charges through tariff for the year.
